That is walk-away territory: no Vendor IP indemnity plus a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services. We therefore insert the preferred Vendor defence and indemnity (IP infringement of the Services or Deliverables, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused unauthorized access to Customer Data, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with a notice/control/cooperation procedure, and narrow our indemnity to Customer-provided content and our breach of Applicable Law. verification.notes: All ten preferred elements are met in operative language: the inserted paragraph creates an express Vendor defend/indemnify/hold-harmless duty to Customer and its Affiliates covering IP infringement of the Services or any Deliverable, Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data, and Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with a notice / control-of-defence / reasonable-cooperation procedure, and § 20.1 is narrowed to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of Applicable Law. The redline is position-complete at the preferred level. The fallback level is not met and does not need to be: the rendered text contains no procure-continued-use / modify / replace remedy, no refund of applicable fees where those remedies are unavailable, and no 3x annual-fee super-cap on Vendor's indemnity. The three 'may exclude' items (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) are permissive allowances rather than obligations, so their absence is Customer-favourable, but the three affirmative fallback requirements are simply missing. If the drafter ever needs to fall back, the operative text must add: (i) 'Vendor shall, at its expense, procure the right to continue use, modify, or replace the infringing item, and if none is commercially reasonable, refund fees paid for the affected Services'; and (ii) an express '3x the fees paid in the twelve months preceding the claim' super-cap. Minimality holds. The only changes are the narrowing edit required by the Customer-indemnity element and a concise insertion for a wholly missing Vendor indemnity; the drafter retained the existing 'defend, indemnify, and hold harmless' formulation, added no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no extra damages categories, and no procedure or boilerplate beyond the notice/control/cooperation mechanic the preferred checklist expressly requires. Omitting 'reasonable attorneys' fees' from the model language does not defeat any element. Intent is preserved: § 9.3's termination trigger, the § 20 heading structure, and unrelated allocation and remedies survive without contradiction, and no favourable Customer language was deleted. Two drafting hygiene points to raise with the counterparty rather than defects in the elements: (a) § 9.3 still cross-refers to 'the remedies required by Section 20.5', which does not exist — this dangling reference pre-dates the redline, but the insertion is the natural place to cure it (numbering the new paragraph and adding the procure/modify/replace/refund ladder as 20.5 would fix both); and (b) the insertion uses capitalised 'Affiliates', 'Customer Data' and 'Deliverable' — confirm each is a defined term in the Definitions article, and if 'Affiliate' is not defined, use lower-case 'affiliates' to avoid introducing an undefined term.

quote: 14.1 As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services. No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.
rationale: The IP package meets our preferred position, not merely the fallback. Section 14.2 gives Customer ownership of each Deliverable created specifically for it and contains an express present assignment by Vendor of all worldwide right, title, and interest (plus equivalent assignments from Vendor personnel). Section 14.3 confines Vendor's retained rights to "Vendor Technology," defined in Section 1.8 as Vendor's pre-existing technology and expressly excluding Customer Data and IP Customer owned before the Effective Date, and routes embedded Vendor Technology to the Section 13.2 licence back, which is "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid" to use, modify, create derivative works from and permit contractors to support for Customer's business — covering the perpetual, irrevocable and royalty-free elements. Section 14.1 confirms Customer owns all Customer Data and Customer-provided material, and the only right passing to Vendor is the limited right to process it solely to provide, secure, support and improve the Services for Customer, which is service delivery rather than independent exploitation; Section 15.1 reinforces this by barring sale, advertising use, data commingling and model training absent our express written consent (a consent gate, not a standing licence). Section 14.4 creates no jointly owned IP unless both Parties sign a separate instrument identifying exploitation rights, which we control. No provision assigns Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor, so there is no walk-away exposure. Two adjacent points are noted only, not redlined here: Section 13.1's revocable, non-transferable Services licence excluding Affiliates and contractors is a Services-access problem for the LICENSE rule (and is partly answered by Section 13.3), and Section 11.1's immediate deletion language is a TRANSITION issue; neither dilutes the ownership and Customer Data direction this rule tests, and we do not flag the same term twice.

quote: 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates.
rationale: Section 24 meets the preferred position in full: 24.1 lets Customer assign to an Affiliate or to an M&A/asset-sale successor without Vendor's consent (Affiliate is broadly defined at 1.1 by >50% control or power to direct management); 24.2 bars Vendor from assigning, delegating material performance, or transferring by change of control without Customer's prior written consent, subject only to a reasonableness standard, and bars assignment to a direct Customer competitor; 24.3 applies a mutual not-unreasonably-withheld consent standard to other assignments; and 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service on Customer's change of control. Section 13.3 reinforces our licence-transfer right on a permitted assignment. Only minor sub-elements fall short of ideal wording — the competitor bar is framed as "without Customer's consent" rather than absolute, and the reasonableness qualifier in 24.2 is keyed to an assignee with adequate capability and financial standing — which we note but do not redline given consent is required for every Vendor assignment in any event. No walk-away features (no blanket bar on Customer assignment, no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right) are present.

rationale: Searches for "liquidated", "penalty", "early termination fee", acceleration and shortfall language return no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalty anywhere in the Agreement. The termination architecture affirmatively confirms the preferred position: § 9.4 limits Customer's exposure on convenience termination to Fees for conforming Services rendered through the effective date with a refund of prepaid Fees; § 27.3 permits termination for prolonged force majeure "without penalty"; § 7.3 bars interest on amounts ultimately found not due; and § 21.3 treats Customer's payment of undisputed Fees as a debt rather than damages. No early-termination fee mechanic exists, so the fallback cap is unnecessary. The take-or-pay minimum in § 2.1 is a volume commitment rather than a stipulated damages amount and is addressed under MINCOMMIT; we do not flag it twice here. This clause set meets the preferred position, so no redline is proposed.

quote: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor. rationale: Section 9.4 satisfies every preferred element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or any Order Form for convenience on thirty days' written notice, Vendor must promptly refund prepaid Fees allocable to the post-termination period, and Vendor is expressly denied a corresponding convenience right during a committed term. The one tension is § 2.1's three-year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights", which cuts against the § 9.4 exit economics; that is the minimum-commitment bargain and is addressed under MINCOMMIT rather than flagged twice here. No redline proposed.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 Excluded Claims expressly covers "data-protection, or security obligations", which the new 21.1 carve-out lifts out of the cap.

elements.element: Indemnification obligations are uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 includes "its indemnification obligations" within Excluded Claims; 21.1's "Except for Excluded Claims" removes them from the cap (the prior "without exception" override is deleted).

elements.element: Gross negligence is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 Excluded Claims: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud"; excepted from the 21.1 cap.

elements.element: Wilful misconduct is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 lists "wilful misconduct" among Excluded Claims, which 21.1 now excepts from the cap.

elements.element: Fraud is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 lists "fraud" among Excluded Claims, excepted from the revised 21.1 cap.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 includes "infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property" in Excluded Claims, now excepted from the cap.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: 21.3 only says "Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services is not damages". "Fees" under s.1.5 excludes taxes, reimbursable expenses, interest and any one-time implementation charge, and the sentence is further narrowed to undisputed amounts for conforming Services — a subset, not Customer's payment obligations as a whole. Repair by amending 21.3 to "Customer's obligations to pay any amounts due under this Agreement are not damages and are not limited by this Section."

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Revised 21.1 caps "each Party's aggregate liability"; symmetrical on its face.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Revised 21.1: "Fees actually paid in the twelve (12) months preceding the event" — a 12-month fee basis; "Fees" per s.1.5 is recurring subscription, professional services and usage fees, so the cap is not illusory. "Actually paid" versus "paid or payable" is a preferred-level shortfall only.

elements.element: Indemnification obligations are uncapped.
elements.evidence: "Except for Excluded Claims" in 21.1 plus 21.3's "its indemnification obligations"; the prior "without exception" that neutralised 21.3 has been removed.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 Excluded Claims includes "breach of confidentiality... obligations", now carved out of the 21.1 cap.

elements.element: Gross negligence is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 Excluded Claims includes "gross negligence"; excepted from the cap by revised 21.1.

elements.element: Wilful misconduct is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 Excluded Claims includes "wilful misconduct"; excepted from the cap by revised 21.1.

verification.notes: Original 21.1 failed the fallback on two material terms: a one-month fee cap (below the 6-month walk-away floor) and "without exception", which overrode the 21.3 Excluded Claims and pulled indemnities, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct inside the cap. The "deviation" classification is correct. The single replace to 21.1 achieves a complete fallback position: mutual cap, 12-month fee basis, and an "Except for Excluded Claims" hook onto the already-favourable 21.3 definition, which supplies the indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct carve-outs. Preferred is not reached. Two defects remain in operative language: (i) 21.1 lacks the "greater of ... and USD 1,000,000" floor and uses "actually paid" rather than "paid or payable", anchored to "the event" rather than the event giving rise to the claim; and (ii) 21.3's payment sentence covers only "undisputed Fees for conforming Services", a narrow subset of the s.1.5 Fees definition, so Customer's payment obligations generally are not excluded from capped damages. Minimality holds: the edit changes only the cap basis and adds the Excluded Claims exception, deletes only the "without exception" language that defeats the carve-out elements, and adds no survival tail, expense language, procedure or extra damages category. Favourable retained text in 21.2 (mutual indirect-damages exclusion; restoration/replacement/notification/incident-response costs as direct damages) and 21.3 is untouched. Intent is preserved: "Excluded Claims" was already defined in 21.3 and already referenced in 21.2, so the new cross-reference creates no undefined term or dangling reference, and no retained sentence contradicts the revised cap. Optional preferred-level upgrade if negotiable: amend 21.1 to "the greater of (a) the Fees paid or payable by Customer in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000", and broaden the 21.3 payment sentence to all amounts due under the Agreement.
